title: Rainbow independent review round 2: gameplay & fairness critic
prompt:
You are an independent, blind gameplay critic for the browser game "Rainbow Bullet Hell Space Princess" in this repository (kind_robots). The owner has designated fresh agent sessions like you as the independent reviewers for its playtest-readiness gate. You have no prior context on purpose: judge only what the game actually does on main, not what anyone claims.

Scope: READ-ONLY review. Do not change game code, do not open pull requests, do not deploy or publish anything. Your only write is your report (below).

The game: engine in utils/arcade/games/rainbowPrincessPreview.ts plus utils/arcade/games/rainbow*.ts. It is a deterministic 60 Hz simulation: createRainbowPrincessPreview({players, rng, sound, hiScore, demo}) then game.update(input) / game.render(ctx), with game.snapshot exposing state. utils/scripts/verifyRainbow*.test.ts show how to drive it headless (npx tsx <file>), and utils/scripts/arcadeCabinetFixture.mjs plus the *.browser.test.mjs files show how to run the real cabinet in Chromium with Playwright (pre-installed; require('playwright'), chromium.launch()). Take screenshots of real play as evidence.

Your lens (from the acceptance criteria, issue silasfelinus/kind_robots#4146 sections 4 and 9; read the issue with gh api repos/silasfelinus/kind_robots/issues/4146 --jq .body): enemy and pattern indistinguishability, copy-paste enemy AI, monotonous stage rhythm, poor tutorial/onboarding, illegible bullet clusters, bullet spam, boss HP padding / damage sponges, unfair or unreadable deaths (no visible tell, no feasible gap), unclear weapon/loadout tradeoffs, exploits (idle/hide spots, spawn collisions), 1-player vs 4-player readability and scaling. Play it adversarially: write scripted input policies that try to die, hide, idle, never use supers, spam supers, and play well; fly several Acts and bosses with 1 and 4 players and multiple seeds.

Report: write projects-review/rainbow-gameplay-critic-round2.md (with any screenshots under projects-review/rainbow-gameplay-critic-round2/, keep them small) and commit + push to your branch claude/rainbow-review2-gameplay. Start with a short verdict, then a table of defects, each with: id, severity (blocker / major / minor), seed, Act/stage, player count and pilots, the defect, exact reproduction (input policy and frame), evidence, and a suggested fix. Then list what you checked and found fine. Be specific and candid; a short list of real, reproducible defects beats a long list of opinions. When done, if you have a send_message tool, send a one-paragraph summary with your branch name to session <the coordinating session id>.
